text: Students should not assume that they will be automatically dropped from their courses for non-payment. Students are solely responsible for ensuring that they have successfully dropped their courses in order to avoid additional fees and charges to their account and to avoid receiving a grade of 'F' for nonattendance. To drop a course(s) after Census Day is considered a withdrawal.
source_title: Office of the Registrar: Dropping a Class

text: Undergraduate students who are receiving financial aid or are international students should be sure to contact their financial aid or international student advisor BEFORE dropping. All new students, freshmen, students with undeclared majors and students who have holds must have their advisor's approval before changing their schedule or completely withdrawing. Before Census Day (see the Academic Calendar) AND if you do not have holds, the preferred method to drop your course(s) is online (see the Guide for Dropping Classes). Students with holds should send the request by email from their UT Dallas account to their academic advisor. The schedule change request must include: your name; the course(s) you are adjusting (adding, dropping or withdrawing); the last four digits of your student ID; and your signature (by email from your UT Dallas account to your academic advisor).
source_title: Office of the Registrar: Dropping a Class
section_heading: Undergraduate Students: Dropping Before Census Day

text: After Census Day through the last day for Withdraw (please see the Academic Calendar), undergraduate students use the new Online Drop/Withdrawal Process for Undergraduate Students. Email requests from your UT Dallas email address will be honored as your signature/consent. Requests made by email are subject to the published deadline dates listed in the academic calendar. You are responsible for all changes to your schedule. Please follow up on your request by logging into Orion and verifying the changes have been made.
source_title: Office of the Registrar: Dropping a Class
section_heading: Undergraduate Students: Dropping After Census Day

text: As enacted by the State of Texas Legislature, undergraduate students will not be permitted to withdraw from more than six courses, including any course from which a transfer student has withdrawn at another institution of higher education in Texas. This rule is effective beginning with first-time freshmen in Fall 2007 and applies when a student: withdrew from the course without receiving a grade or incurring an academic penalty; has a transcript that indicates or will indicate that the student was enrolled in the course; and is not withdrawing from the course in order to withdraw from the institution. Non-academic withdrawals are exempt from counting toward the six drop rule.
source_title: Office of the Registrar: Dropping a Class
section_heading: Limitations on Course Withdrawals for Undergraduate Students (Texas 6-Withdrawals Rule)

text: Graduate students who are receiving financial aid or are international students should be sure to contact their financial aid or international student advisor BEFORE dropping. Before Census Day (see the Academic Calendar), graduate students can drop their course(s) online (see the Guide for Dropping Classes) or by email from their UT Dallas account to records@utdallas.edu. The schedule change request must include: your name; the course(s) you are adjusting (adding, dropping or withdrawing); the last four digits of your student ID; and your signature.
source_title: Office of the Registrar: Dropping a Class
section_heading: Graduate Students: Dropping Before Census Day

text: After Census Day through the last day for Withdraw (W), graduate students should email the academic advisor from their UT Dallas email account with the course to withdraw, or fill out the Registration form (pdf) and submit it to the academic advisor. Email requests from your UT Dallas email address will be honored as your signature/consent. Requests made by email are subject to the published deadline dates listed in the academic calendar. You are responsible for all changes to your schedule. Please follow up on your request by logging into Orion and verifying the changes have been made.
source_title: Office of the Registrar: Dropping a Class
section_heading: Graduate Students: Withdrawing After Census Day

text: Please visit the Bursar's Office website for information regarding refunds for dropped classes.
